# NurseryTech Review: Three Baby Monitors Tested for Privacy, Battery, and Range

We tested all three monitors over five nights each in a two-story, 2,400 sq ft house
with a backyard, walking each parent unit away from its camera in 50-foot increments
until the picture broke up or froze, and running each parent unit from a full charge
until it powered off to measure real-world battery life. We also mapped each unit's
network architecture: does video ever leave the house over the internet, or does it
stay on a local link?

**Range walk-test (feet from camera to last clean picture):**

| Monitor | Measured range | Architecture |
|---|---|---|
| NestView Local | 980 ft | Local FHSS radio link — never touches the internet |
| PeekaPod Smart | N/A — wifi/cloud, not a fixed-range device | Wifi to router, then internet to PeekaPod's cloud servers, then to your phone |
| GuardianEye Duo | 690 ft | Local FHSS radio link — never touches the internet |

**Battery rundown (parent unit, screen on, standard use):**

| Monitor | Measured runtime |
|---|---|
| NestView Local | 14h 40m, close to the published 15-hour spec |
| PeekaPod Smart | Not applicable — your phone is the parent unit, running on your phone's own battery |
| GuardianEye Duo | 7h 50m, close to the published 8-hour spec |

**Privacy architecture:** The NestView and GuardianEye are both closed local systems —
video never leaves the house, there's no account, and a home internet outage has no
effect on either. The PeekaPod is a cloud product: video is streamed off the camera,
through your home network, and through PeekaPod's servers before it reaches your phone,
which means it needs a working internet connection to work at all, and your video does
pass through a third party's infrastructure along the way.

**Verdict:** For a buyer who specifically wants local-only video with no internet
dependency, at least 12 hours of parent-unit battery, and 900+ feet of range, the
NestView Local is the only one of the three that clears all three bars. The GuardianEye
matches it on privacy architecture but falls short on both battery (8h) and range
(690 ft measured). The PeekaPod doesn't compete on this buyer's terms at all — it's a
capable app-based monitor, but it is fundamentally an internet-dependent product.
